entities.summary:
Burgundofara, also Saint Fara or Fare, was the founder and first abbess of the Abbey of Faremoutiers, a medieval Benedictine convent established in 651 CE in what is now the commune of Saint-Fargeau, Seine-et-Marne, Île-de-France, France.

This abbess played a pivotal role in the early Christianization of the region, serving as a spiritual leader and educator for the local population. Her influence extended beyond the abbey's walls, shaping the spiritual and cultural landscape of the surrounding area.

The Abbey of Faremoutiers would go on to become a major center of learning and spirituality, attracting scholars and pilgrims from across Europe. Burgundofara's legacy as a pioneering female leader and educator would be remembered for centuries to come, inspiring future generations of women in leadership roles.

As a testament to her enduring impact, the Abbey of Faremoutiers remains an important historical site in France, attracting visitors from around the world who come to marvel at its stunning architecture and rich history.
